concept.name: Resistance
concept.definition: A price level or zone at which selling is thought to be strong enough to prevent the price from rising further. It is a core hypothesis of technical analysis about where supply concentrates, not a guaranteed ceiling.
concept.intuition: As price gets more expensive, sellers become more willing to sell and buyers less willing to buy, so rallies tend to stall there.
concept.mechanics: Commonly established at previous reaction highs or at broken support levels (polarity principle: broken support can turn into resistance and vice versa, often because trapped holders sell at breakeven on the return). A decisive break above is read as demand overcoming supply.
concept.failure_modes: Resistance breaks happen regularly; price can also briefly exceed the level intraday and fall back, so marginal penetrations are unreliable as signals.
concept.misconceptions: That resistance must repel price on the first approach; levels are zones of probable supply, and repeated tests often weaken them.
concept.example: ChartSchool documents Halliburton's broken support at 42.5 turning into resistance: the stock rallied back to 42.5 three times and failed each time.
